app-server.title: Add a copy
app-server.why: A second one appears, wired up like the first, and takes half the requests. In a real system a load balancer in front shares them out.

app-server.title: Learn why copies need a load balancer
app-server.why: Copies only help if something shares the requests out between them, and skips any copy that breaks.

function.title: Add a copy
function.why: A second one appears, wired up like the first, and takes half the work.

worker.title: Add a copy
worker.why: A second worker appears, taking tasks from the same queue, so twice as many get done.

worker.title: Learn how queues and workers fit together
worker.why: The queue holds tasks while workers are busy, so nobody waits for them.

sql-database.title: Put a cache in front of it
sql-database.why: Add a Cache and connect the server to it: most reads are then answered from fast memory, and far fewer reach the database.

sql-database.title: Add a read replica
sql-database.why: Add a second SQL Database, connect the server to both, and a cable from the main one to the copy. Reads are shared; the main one keeps the writes.

sql-database.title: Split the data across databases
sql-database.why: Put a Shard Router in front of several databases, each holding part of the data (sharding). A bigger step, for when the others aren't enough.

nosql-database.title: Add a copy
nosql-database.why: A second one appears, wired up like the first, and takes half the work.

nosql-database.title: Put a cache in front of it
nosql-database.why: Add a Cache and connect the server to it, so most reads never reach the database.

search-index.title: Add a copy

external-service.title: Call it from the background, through a queue
external-service.why: Put a Queue and Workers between your server and this service: only actions reach it, at a pace it can take, instead of every request.
